risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Given operations in long-distance transportation, warehousing, cargo handling and movement of diverse consignments including hazardous and chemical goods, road accidents, driver fatigue, workplace incidents and health-related risks may adversely impact employees, business continuity, operational efficiency and stakeholder confidence. Mitigation is an EHS framework with PPE, driver and employee safety training, stringent cargo-handling protocols, 24x7 GPS-enabled fleet monitoring through centralised control towers, medical/insurance cover and the TCI Safe Safar driver initiative.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across long-haul transport, warehousing and hazardous-cargo handling

risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: inability to attract, develop and retain skilled talent may impact operational efficiency, service quality, productivity and the Company's ability to meet customer expectations and growth objectives. Mitigated through structured learning and development, job rotation, upskilling/reskilling, leadership development, performance-based progression, recognition programmes, ESOPs and academic/industry partnerships for a talent pipeline.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications — worldwide businesses have reported newer and emerging cybersecurity threats such as ransomware, posing risk to everyday business operations. The Company states it has adequate cyber and IT security systems including ITDR, verified by external consultants with all recommendations implemented. Exposure is structurally rising as operations become dependent on proprietary TMS/WMS, control towers and digital documentation.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: climate change can impact operations through extreme weather events such as cyclones, heat waves and floods, which have the potential to create severe disruptions to a pan-India road, rail and coastal network (the mitigation text is truncated in the routed source).
risks.risk: Climate change and extreme weather disruption

risks.note: The MD&A records that the US-Israel and Iran conflict, escalating since February 2026, has hit critical maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, forcing vessel rerouting, suspended operations and a surge in war-risk surcharges and insurance premiums; Gulf airspace closures cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%; and energy-market volatility spiked bunker fuel prices, creating cascading cost pressure across supply chains. Coastal shipping and cross-border operations sit directly in this exposure.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to trade lanes, energy and freight costs

risks.note: The BRSR workforce table shows Nil permanent workers against 8,904 workers who are 'other than permanent', alongside 4,165 permanent employees. Service quality, safety compliance and cost are therefore delivered largely through a non-permanent workforce and vendor/driver ecosystem the Company does not employ directly.
risks.risk: Structural dependence on a contract/outsourced workforce

risks.note: Exports contribute only 0.18% of total turnover and international presence is limited to three countries (Bangladesh, Nepal, UAE) with no international offices reported in the BRSR operations table, so earnings are tied almost entirely to Indian freight, warehousing and coastal demand cycles despite the Company's stated global-connectivity ambition.

The MD&A states that logistics digitalisation has shifted from a competitive advantage to a fundamental operational requirement and that organisations failing to embed technology into core workflows now operate at a structural disadvantage, with ~70% of logistics enterprises accelerating digital transformation — implying continuous, non-discretionary technology spend simply to hold position.
risks.risk: Competitive/technology displacement as digitalisation becomes the baseline
